data.narrative:
Hadrian, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company, carries a current post-money valuation of $1.6B after raising $560M to date. The valuation assessment draws on a comparable universe of nine private peers and one public company (277810.KQ), all operating in robotics and manufacturing at Series B through Series D stages.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C to Series D advancement, yielding $2.7B. Peer-median methodology examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—Exotec ($2.0B Series D), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C)—producing a median of $1.7B with a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. This peer cohort establishes valuation bounds across stage transitions within the sector.

The triangulated range supports a median valuation of $2.2B, with a low of $1.4B and a high of $3.1B. The gap between peer-median ($1.7B) and stage-progression ($2.7B) reflects uncertainty around both the sustainability of historical step-up multiples and Hadrian's relative competitive positioning within its peer set. Key variables affecting resolution include near-term funding round dynamics, margin trajectory, and customer concentration relative to comparables.
